safety_note.ru: Переосмысление нельзя использовать для отрицания реальной опасности, насилия, медицинских симптомов или необходимости действовать.

title.en: Reinterpret meaning to change subjective emotion
title.ru: Переосмысливайте значение для изменения субъективной эмоции

action.en: State the current interpretation and one observable prediction. Check available evidence and generate a realistic alternative meaning without denying danger or loss. Compare the predicted feeling, action, and consequence with what actually happens; if meaning is not the active link, test another channel.
action.ru: Сформулируйте текущую интерпретацию и один наблюдаемый прогноз. Проверьте доступные факты и создайте реалистичный альтернативный смысл, не отрицая опасность или потерю. Сравните ожидаемое переживание, действие и последствие с тем, что произошло; если смысл не является действующим звеном, проверяйте другой канал.

applicability.en: Ordinary low-risk situations with uncertain or incomplete interpretations and an observable way to check the prediction.
applicability.ru: Обычные низкорисковые ситуации с неопределённой или неполной интерпретацией и наблюдаемым способом проверить прогноз.

evidence_basis.en: Randomized reappraisal instructions reduce reported negative emotion in bounded laboratory tasks, while appraisal-emotion associations and the proposed coordination mechanism do not guarantee the same effect in daily life.
evidence_basis.ru: Рандомизированные инструкции переоценки уменьшают сообщаемую негативную эмоцию в ограниченных лабораторных заданиях, но связи оценки с эмоцией и предполагаемый механизм координации не гарантируют такой же эффект в повседневной жизни.

expected_change.en: Possibly lower self-reported negative emotion or a different available action in situations where the original interpretation is incomplete and a credible alternative can be tested.
expected_change.ru: Возможно меньшее субъективное негативное переживание или появление другого доступного действия в ситуациях, где исходная интерпретация неполна и реалистичную альтернативу можно проверить.

not_established.en: Reappraisal is not universally better than acceptance, problem solving, exposure, support, environmental change, or protection, and it need not change physiology or feeling for every person.
not_established.ru: Переоценка не всегда лучше принятия, решения проблемы, экспозиции, поддержки, изменения среды или защиты и не обязана менять физиологию или переживание у каждого человека.

practical_question.en: When might checking the meaning of a situation help?
practical_question.ru: Когда может помочь проверка смысла ситуации?

safety_note.en: Do not reinterpret away credible danger, abuse, urgent medical symptoms, or another person's boundary.
safety_note.ru: Не переосмысливайте как несущественные реальную опасность, насилие, срочные медицинские симптомы или границы другого человека.

title.en: Test a truthful reinterpretation as one possible route
title.ru: Проверьте правдивое переосмысление как один из возможных путей

question.en: Does meaning reinterpretation causally mediate changes in experience, physiology, and behavior during reappraisal?
question.ru: Является ли переосмысление значения причинным посредником изменений переживания, физиологии и поведения при переоценке?

what_would_help.en: Experiments that independently perturb reinterpretation, measure the mediator before outcomes, and test alternative pathways across modalities.
what_would_help.ru: Эксперименты, независимо изменяющие переосмысление, измеряющие посредник до результатов и проверяющие альтернативные пути по нескольким модальностям.

why_open.en: Reappraisal instructions change several outcomes, but correlations or statistical mediation do not isolate reinterpretation as the causal process.
why_open.ru: Инструкции по переоценке меняют несколько результатов, но корреляции и статистическая медиация не выделяют переосмысление как причинный процесс.

sources.authority_note: Foundational randomized experiment separating experience, expression, and physiological response channels.
sources.title: Antecedent- and response-focused emotion regulation: divergent consequences for experience, expression, and physiology

sources.authority_note: Randomized multimodal comparison of reappraisal, acceptance, and natural viewing.
sources.title: Cognitive reappraisal and acceptance: an experimental comparison of two emotion regulation strategies

sources.authority_note: Primary fMRI experiment applying multilevel mediation, included with explicit noncausal interpretation limits.
sources.title: Neural mechanisms of emotion regulation: Evidence for two independent prefrontal-subcortical pathways

sources.authority_note: Recent randomized multimodal experiment preserving divergence between subjective and psychophysiological outcomes.
sources.title: Cognitive reappraisal and acceptance following acute stress

families.title: Cognitive reappraisal

confidence.rationale: Major component reviews converge on separating response systems, while theories disagree about their causal organization and the primacy of conscious feeling.

limitations: This representation organizes measurement and does not establish that one component causes the others or that every episode contains every component.
claims.plain_language_summary: An emotion is not only a word such as “fear” or one intensity score. For practical analysis, separate what happened, what it meant to the person, what they felt, what changed in the body, what they were inclined to do, what they actually did, and what followed. This does not assume that every component appears or changes together.

scope.population: Humans experiencing or reporting time-bounded emotional events.
scope.temporal_scope: Seconds to minutes within an emotional episode.

claims.statement: An emotion episode should be represented as a time-varying set of experiential, physiological, action-related, and expressive components in context rather than as one interchangeable score or label.

confidence.rationale: The measurement review found unique variance and limited convergence across experiential, physiological, and behavioral systems, although each method also has specific limitations.

limitations: Self-report is the most direct available measure of conscious feeling but is not a complete measure of physiology, behavior, or an unreported process.
claims.plain_language_summary: A person can report less distress while heart rate, skin conductance, facial expression, or behavior changes differently. Therefore decide in advance what outcome matters and measure that channel directly; do not use a calm face as proof of a calm feeling or one bodily signal as the emotion itself.

scope.population: Humans measured during laboratory or naturalistic emotional events represented in the review literature.
scope.temporal_scope: Measurement within or after a declared emotional episode.

claims.statement: Self-reported feeling, physiology, expressive behavior, action, and observer labels measure different aspects of an emotional episode and no single channel is a universal gold standard for the others.

confidence.rationale: A large mixed-effects meta-analysis synthesized 2,634 effects from 309 studies, but heterogeneous terminology, retrospective self-report, shared method, and noncausal designs limit mechanistic interpretation.

claims.confounding_note: Shared self-report method, retrospective reconstruction, emotion-label semantics, event selection, culture, and study design can produce or alter appraisal-emotion associations.

estimate.metric: mean correlation for previously hypothesized appraisal-emotion relationships
estimate.notes: Seventy-five percent of previously hypothesized relationships were statistically significant; unpredicted relationships averaged r = .27.

limitations: Correlation does not show that a measured appraisal uniquely caused the emotion, nor that changing one appraisal will reliably change every response channel.
claims.plain_language_summary: How people evaluate relevance, control, certainty, responsibility, effort, and pleasantness is systematically related to what emotions they report. The profiles overlap and much evidence is correlational, so an appraisal is a useful hypothesis to check, not a hidden cause that can be read from the emotion label.

boundary_conditions: Forty-seven appraisal dimensions, 63 emotions, heterogeneous measures, and the study designs included by Yeo and Ong.
scope.population: Human participants represented in 309 appraisal-emotion studies across 251 reports.
scope.temporal_scope: Event appraisal and reported emotion in experimental, recalled, and other study contexts included in the meta-analysis.

claims.statement: Across the studies synthesized by Yeo and Ong, measured appraisal dimensions were systematically associated with reported emotions, but the profiles were overlapping and included many relationships not uniquely predicted in advance.

confidence.rationale: Experimental appraisal manipulations and component findings constrain the theory, but comprehensive tests of temporal coordination, mediation, and alternatives remain incomplete.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The account is weakened when independently manipulated appraisal dimensions fail to alter predicted later components, or when competing bodily, perceptual, learning, or constructionist models explain the temporal data better.
limitations: The review supports a research programme and partial predictions, not one universally established causal sequence for all emotions.
claims.plain_language_summary: One working model says that changing evaluation of an event can reorganize action readiness, bodily response, expression, feeling, and later action over time. The whole loop is not yet one established mechanism. In practice, change one candidate link and check whether the predicted channel changes before accepting the explanation.

boundary_conditions: Repeated, independently operationalized appraisal and response-component measurements with explicit temporal ordering.
scope.population: Humans in appraisal and emotion-process studies.
scope.temporal_scope: Dynamic unfolding of an emotional episode over seconds to minutes.

claims.statement: Changes in multi-level appraisal may help organize the unfolding pattern of action tendency, physiology, expression, feeling, and overt action during an emotion episode.
claims.temporal_ordering: The theory predicts appraisal changes that precede or recursively interact with later component changes, but many studies measure appraisal and feeling retrospectively at the same time.

families.description: Relevant event, appraisal, feeling, physiology, action tendency, expression, overt action, measurement, and proposed coordination kept distinct.

evidence.design: Mixed-effects meta-analysis of 2,634 effect sizes from 309 studies across 251 reports, covering 47 appraisal dimensions, 63 emotions, and 853 specific relationships.

effect.metric: mean correlation for previously hypothesized appraisal-emotion relationships
effect.notes: 75.0% of hypothesized relationships were statistically significant; unpredicted relationships averaged r = .27.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting the mixed-effects synthesis, study and effect counts, and mean correlations for predicted and unpredicted appraisal-emotion relationships.
limitations: The abstract-level extraction does not re-grade every included study, and shared method, retrospective designs, heterogeneity, and publication selection limit causal interpretation.
evidence.population: Human participants in the appraisal-emotion studies included by Yeo and Ong.
evidence.summary: Appraisal dimensions showed systematic but nonunique associations with reported emotions across a large heterogeneous literature.

evidence.design: Integrative review emphasizing experimental emotion research and neighboring domains relevant to elicitation, action tendencies, physiology, expression, feeling, and labeling.
evidence.extraction_locator: Abstract and review synthesis describing event appraisal, component differentiation, interactions, and unresolved temporal coordination.
limitations: A narrative review of heterogeneous studies cannot by itself establish the complete appraisal-to-component causal architecture.
evidence.population: Human emotion studies reviewed by the authors.
evidence.summary: The review reports evidence compatible with appraisal-related component differentiation while identifying interactions, timing, and synchronization as unresolved mechanism problems.

boundary_notes: The same event need not be emotionally relevant to every person or on every occasion.
objects.definition: An internal or external event that is potentially relevant to a person's goals, needs, values, relationships, or safety in a declared situation.
objects.label: Emotion-relevant event
objects.scope: Time-bounded human emotional episodes represented by the included literature.

boundary_notes: An emotion word or questionnaire score is not the complete episode.
The components can differ in timing, intensity, and direction and need not form one invariant package.
This component definition does not decide among appraisal, basic-emotion, constructionist, interoceptive, or learning accounts of emotion causation.
objects.definition: A time-bounded, person-in-context process involving some combination of appraisal, subjective experience, physiological change, action tendency, expression, and overt action.
objects.label: Emotion episode

boundary_notes: Appraisal can be rapid, automatic, or partly outside awareness and is not limited to deliberate verbal thought.
Appraisal dimensions and terminology differ across theories and studies.
A profile inferred only from an emotion label is circular and is not an independent measurement.
objects.definition: A pattern of evaluated meaning dimensions such as goal relevance, pleasantness, certainty, control, agency, anticipated effort, and compatibility with current concerns.
objects.label: Event appraisal profile

boundary_notes: Subjective feeling is not interchangeable with autonomic activity, facial expression, or an observer's emotion label.
objects.definition: The time-indexed conscious experience of affect or emotion reported by a person during or after an event.
objects.label: Subjective emotional feeling

boundary_notes: Different physiological channels need not covary or uniquely identify a named emotion.
objects.definition: Time-indexed autonomic, endocrine, respiratory, or other bodily change measured during an emotion-relevant event.
objects.label: Emotion-related physiological response

boundary_notes: A tendency is not the same as an observed action and may be inhibited, redirected, or never performed.
objects.definition: A context-sensitive readiness or inclination toward a class of actions, such as approach, withdrawal, attack, freezing, support seeking, or repair.
objects.label: Emotion-related action tendency

objects.definition: Observable facial, vocal, postural, or gestural behavior occurring during an emotion-relevant event.
objects.function_note: Expression can communicate, regulate interaction, or reflect response preparation, but its function cannot be inferred from appearance alone.
objects.label: Emotion-related expression
objects.response_topography: Protocol-defined facial, vocal, postural, or gestural change.

objects.definition: Observable action taken during or after an emotion-relevant event that may alter the situation, the person's exposure, or social feedback.
objects.function_note: Similar-looking actions can serve different functions and the same feeling can precede different actions.
objects.label: Emotion-related overt action
objects.response_topography: Study- or person-specific approach, avoidance, communication, inhibition, or problem-solving action.

boundary_notes: Retrospective reports can reconstruct appraisals after the emotion and do not establish temporal or causal order.
objects.definition: Self-report or structured rating of declared appraisal dimensions for a specific event or recalled episode.
objects.label: Event appraisal report
objects.method: Rate study-defined meaning dimensions independently of the final emotion label where possible.

objects.definition: Self-reported intensity, quality, or category of conscious emotional experience during or after a declared event.
objects.label: Emotional feeling report
objects.method: Use a declared rating scale, emotion vocabulary, timing, and reference period.

objects.definition: Channel-specific recording of bodily responses time-locked to an emotion-relevant event.
objects.label: Emotion-related physiology recording
objects.method: Record and analyze each declared physiological channel with its own baseline, timing, and preprocessing.

objects.definition: Observer or automated coding of declared facial, vocal, postural, or gestural features during an event.
objects.label: Emotion expression coding
objects.method: Apply a declared coding protocol to recorded expressive behavior without treating the code as direct access to subjective feeling.

boundary_notes: The complete coordination loop is a theoretical mechanism, not a direct consequence of appraisal-emotion correlations.
Appraisal need not be conscious or verbal, but calling an unmeasured process automatic does not verify it.
objects.definition: Proposed dynamic process in which evaluations of an event's meaning help organize changing action tendencies, physiology, expression, feeling, and action over time.
objects.label: Appraisal-guided component coordination
realization_conditions: Appraisal and response components are measured repeatedly with sufficient temporal resolution.
Competing bodily, learning, perceptual, and constructionist explanations remain testable.
Component changes are not inferred from one self-report score alone.

action.en: Write one concrete sequence: event and context → interpreted meaning → reported feeling and bodily changes → urge → observed action → immediate and delayed consequences. Mark which entries were observed, self-reported, or only inferred, then select one low-risk link to test.
action.ru: Запишите одну конкретную последовательность: событие и контекст → воспринятый смысл → переживание и телесные изменения → побуждение → наблюдаемое действие → немедленные и отсроченные последствия. Отметьте, что наблюдалось, что сообщено человеком, а что только предполагается, затем выберите одно безопасное звено для проверки.

applicability.en: Low-risk reflection, coaching, education, research formulation, and collaborative clinical assessment when the event can be examined safely.
applicability.ru: Низкорисковая рефлексия, обучение, консультирование, исследовательская формулировка и совместная клиническая оценка, когда эпизод можно безопасно рассматривать.

evidence_basis.en: Component reviews support separating experience, physiology, expression, and behavior; the appraisal meta-analysis supports checking meaning dimensions while not establishing a unique causal sequence.
evidence_basis.ru: Компонентные обзоры поддерживают разделение переживания, физиологии, выражения и поведения; метаанализ оценки ситуации поддерживает проверку смысловых измерений, но не устанавливает единственную причинную последовательность.

expected_change.en: A more precise, testable target such as interpretation, exposure, bodily arousal, action, communication, environmental trigger, or consequence rather than a vague goal to “remove the emotion.”
expected_change.ru: Более точная и проверяемая цель: интерпретация, контакт с ситуацией, телесное возбуждение, действие, общение, средовой триггер или последствие вместо расплывчатой цели «убрать эмоцию».

not_established.en: The map does not diagnose a disorder, prove the appraisal caused the feeling, or show which link should be changed for a particular person.
not_established.ru: Схема не диагностирует расстройство, не доказывает, что оценка ситуации вызвала чувство, и не определяет автоматически, какое звено менять у конкретного человека.

practical_question.en: Where can a difficult emotional episode be changed without assuming one universal cause?
practical_question.ru: На какое звено трудного эмоционального эпизода можно воздействовать, не предполагая единственную универсальную причину?

safety_note.en: Real danger, severe symptoms, trauma, self-harm, violence, or medical symptoms require appropriate protection and qualified assessment rather than self-experiment alone.
safety_note.ru: Реальная опасность, тяжёлые симптомы, травма, самоповреждение, насилие или медицинские симптомы требуют подходящей защиты и квалифицированной оценки, а не только самостоятельного эксперимента.

title.en: Map the emotion episode before choosing an intervention
title.ru: Разберите эмоциональный эпизод до выбора воздействия

question.en: For a particular person and event, which change in appraisal, bodily response, action tendency, behavior, or context causally changes which later emotion component?
question.ru: Какое изменение оценки ситуации, телесной реакции, побуждения, поведения или контекста причинно меняет какой последующий компонент эмоции у конкретного человека и в конкретном событии?

what_would_help.en: Preregistered intensive longitudinal and experimental studies with independent appraisal measures, channel-specific outcomes, temporal ordering, safe sequential interventions, and comparison of appraisal, bodily, learning, and constructionist models.
what_would_help.ru: Пререгистрированные интенсивные продольные и экспериментальные исследования с независимыми измерениями оценки ситуации, отдельными исходами для каждого канала, временным порядком, безопасными последовательными воздействиями и сравнением оценочных, телесных, обучающих и конструкционистских моделей.

why_open.en: Appraisal-emotion associations are broad but nonunique, response channels only partly converge, and most studies do not repeatedly measure and manipulate competing components within the same person.
why_open.ru: Связи оценки ситуации с эмоциями широки, но не однозначны, каналы реакции совпадают лишь частично, а большинство исследований не измеряет и не изменяет конкурирующие компоненты многократно у одного человека.

sources.authority_note: Recent large meta-analysis used for quantitative appraisal-emotion associations, not for causal mechanism claims.
sources.title: Associations between cognitive appraisals and emotions — a meta-analytic review

sources.authority_note: Authoritative process review used to define component distinctions and represent appraisal-driven coordination as a theory requiring further tests.
sources.title: The emotion process — event appraisal and component differentiation

sources.authority_note: Measurement review used to prevent subjective experience, physiology, and behavior from being treated as interchangeable emotion measures.
sources.title: Measures of emotion — a review

families.title: Emotion components and appraisal

claims.causal_estimand: Within-task difference in false-alarm probability for lure versus matched control foils.

confidence.rationale: The within-task lure manipulation directly contrasted trial types, but the result comes from one study and specific verbal task variants.

limitations: Trial sequencing and previous-item history can influence lure effects.
claims.plain_language_summary: In verbal N-back tasks, a lure was a familiar item seen recently but in the wrong serial position. Participants falsely accepted these lures more often than ordinary non-targets, showing that the task requires control over familiarity, not just remembering items.

boundary_conditions: Restricted to the tested n-minus-one lure and control-foil definitions.
Does not identify familiarity control as the unique causal mechanism.
scope.population: Adults completing the verbal N-back experiments reported by Kane et al. 2007.
scope.temporal_scope: Trial-level responses during 2-back and 3-back performance.

claims.statement: In the tested verbal 2-back and 3-back tasks, n-minus-one lure foils increased false alarms relative to matched control foils.
claims.temporal_ordering: Foil type is presented before the participant response on each trial.

confidence.rationale: The result directly challenges simple task interchangeability, but uses one N-back family and one complex-span marker.

claims.confounding_note: Reliability, method variance, and task-specific processes can alter the observed association.

estimate.metric: cross-task association
estimate.notes: PubMed abstract describes the correlation as weak; the numerical estimate was not extracted.

claims.plain_language_summary: People who scored well on verbal N-back were only slightly more likely to score well on operation span. The two tasks therefore should not be treated as interchangeable tests of one working-memory ability.

boundary_conditions: A weak task correlation can reflect reliability and task-specific variance.
scope.population: Adults completing verbal N-back, operation-span, and fluid-intelligence tasks.
scope.temporal_scope: Cross-sectional individual differences within one assessment session.

claims.statement: Verbal N-back performance showed weak convergence with operation-span performance in Kane et al. 2007.

confidence.rationale: Multiple task variants and N=703 reduce single-task contamination, while latent structure remains model- and sample-dependent.

claims.confounding_note: Shared method, stimulus, reliability, and model-selection choices can influence latent relations.

estimate.metric: latent-factor correlation
estimate.notes: Bootstrap confidence interval reported for the relationship between the two latent constructs.

claims.plain_language_summary: In a large task battery, performance on N-back tasks and backward-recall tasks was best described by two related but distinct statistical factors. Calling both “working memory” does not mean they measure exactly the same ability.

boundary_conditions: Factor separation does not prove separate cognitive mechanisms.
Results depend on task selection and latent-model specification.
scope.population: 703 participants completing spatial and verbal N-back, backward-recall, and reasoning tasks.
scope.temporal_scope: Cross-sectional multi-task assessment.

claims.statement: A preregistered large-scale battery was better represented by distinct but related N-back and backward-recall latent factors than by a single working-memory factor.

confidence.rationale: A computational model reproduced selected behavioral patterns, establishing plausibility rather than unique human implementation.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The account is weakened if preregistered task manipulations uniquely requiring active cross-trial maintenance outperform episodic-retrieval models under matched complexity.
limitations: Computational fit is not direct process measurement.
claims.plain_language_summary: A computational model reproduced important N-back results by retrieving recent episodes rather than relying only on a fixed-capacity working-memory store. This shows that episodic retrieval is a viable explanation, not that the brain uses only this mechanism during N-back.

boundary_conditions: Does not show that working-memory retention never contributes in humans.
Generalization to other task variants requires testing.
scope.population: Computational account fitted to qualitative patterns from human N-back performance.
scope.temporal_scope: Sequential item presentation and response within N-back tasks.

claims.statement: Episodic retrieval can, in principle, support N-back set-size and lure effects without trial-to-trial retention in a capacity-limited working-memory store.
claims.temporal_ordering: Current stimuli cue retrieval before the target judgment is emitted.

families.description: N-back performance, construct validity, lure interference, and competing memory mechanisms.

evidence.design: Within-task comparison of n-minus-one lure foils and control foils in verbal 2-back and 3-back tasks.

effect.metric: lure-versus-control false-alarm difference
effect.notes: Lures elicited more false alarms under both tested loads.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract, experimental lure results.
limitations: Numerical effect and sample size were not extracted from the full text.
evidence.population: Adults completing verbal N-back tasks.
evidence.summary: Controlled lure trials increased false alarms relative to control foils.

evidence.design: Correlation of verbal N-back, operation span, and fluid-intelligence performance.

effect.metric: N-back to operation-span correlation
effect.notes: Described as weak in the indexed abstract.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract, correlational construct-validity result.
limitations: One marker task cannot define the full working-memory construct.
evidence.population: Adults completing the combined experimental-correlational battery.
evidence.summary: N-back and operation span did not behave as interchangeable measures of one construct.

evidence.design: Preregistered latent-variable comparison using multiple spatial and verbal N-back and backward-recall tasks.

effect.metric: latent-factor relationship
effect.notes: Best-fitting model separated two related paradigm factors.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract and Figure 3 caption.
limitations: Cross-sectional factor structure does not identify mechanisms.
evidence.population: 703 participants completing the task battery.
evidence.summary: N-back and backward recall formed distinct but related latent factors rather than one interchangeable task factor.

evidence.design: Neural-network model augmented with episodic memory but without cross-trial working-memory retention.

effect.metric: qualitative reproduction of set-size and lure effects
effect.notes: Model reproduced selected empirical patterns without a cross-trial WM retention capacity.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract, computational-model result.
limitations: Model sufficiency does not establish human process identity or exclusivity.
evidence.population: Model evaluated against qualitative set-size and lure effects reported in human N-back research.
evidence.summary: The model demonstrates that episodic retrieval is a viable alternative contributor to canonical N-back effects.

objects.definition: Sequential matching task in which each item is judged against the item presented n positions earlier.

external_mappings.rationale: The external record identifies the N-back task family, while this PMM Context record additionally scopes the variants used by the evidence pack; the Cognitive Atlas page is marked Unreviewed.

objects.label: N-back task context
objects.scope: Human laboratory N-back variants; stimulus domain, load, lure frequency, and scoring can differ.

objects.definition: Assessment context containing multiple task variants used to estimate common and paradigm-specific latent variance.
objects.label: Multi-task working-memory battery
objects.scope: Human psychometric and latent-variable studies using multiple indicators per proposed construct.

boundary_notes: Competing theories disagree about storage, attention, retrieval, and interference contributions.
A score from one task is not identical to the construct.
objects.definition: Limited ability to maintain accessible information while performing goal-directed processing.

external_mappings.rationale: PMM Working-memory capacity is narrower than the RDoC Working Memory construct, which also includes active maintenance, flexible updating, and interference control.
PMM Working-memory capacity is one constrained construct within the broader external working-memory concept; the Cognitive Atlas page is marked Unreviewed.

objects.label: Working-memory capacity

boundary_notes: This is a latent statistical construct, not an identified cognitive mechanism.
objects.definition: Shared individual-difference variance among N-back variants after separating variance common with other working-memory paradigms.
objects.label: N-back-specific performance variance

objects.definition: Momentary graded familiarity elicited by a current item relative to recently encountered items.
objects.label: Familiarity signal during N-back judgment

objects.definition: Observable response classifying the current item as matching or not matching the item n positions earlier.
objects.label: N-back target judgment
objects.response_topography: Button press or equivalent binary response.

objects.definition: Proportion of lure trials incorrectly classified as N-back targets.
objects.label: N-back lure false-alarm rate

objects.definition: Experimental presentation of non-target items matching a recently seen position other than the required n-back position.
objects.delivery: Insert n-minus-one lure foils among matched control foils during 2-back and 3-back tasks.
objects.label: N-back lure-foil manipulation

boundary_notes: Construct validity depends on the inferential use and comparison measures.
objects.definition: Accuracy, false-alarm, miss, or latency scoring obtained from a specified N-back task variant.
objects.label: N-back performance measurement
objects.method: Score responses by trial type, load, and prespecified accuracy or latency rule.

objects.definition: Accuracy or span score for recalling a presented sequence in reverse order.
objects.label: Backward-recall performance measurement
objects.method: Present sequences and score correctly recalled items or spans in reverse order.

objects.definition: Complex-span score derived from remembering items while performing an interleaved processing task.

claims.plain_language_summary: RDoC uses “perception” for processes that turn sensory input into useful representations of the outside world. confidence.rationale: The measurement definition is explicit in a peer-reviewed methods review and is standard for grating contrast psychophysics.

limitations: Reciprocal threshold is an operational measurement and does not identify a unique sensory or neural mechanism.
claims.plain_language_summary: Researchers gradually reduce a pattern’s contrast until it can only just be detected reliably. A lower required contrast means greater sensitivity, so sensitivity is calculated as one divided by that threshold. Repeating this at several stripe widths produces a contrast sensitivity function; the curve is a measurement, not perception itself.

boundary_conditions: Contrast definition, threshold criterion, spatial frequency, stimulus, and viewing conditions must be stated.
scope.population: Observers completing protocol-defined contrast detection or identification tasks.
scope.temporal_scope: Threshold estimation across trials at prespecified spatial frequencies.

claims.statement: In contrast psychophysics, sensitivity is the reciprocal of the contrast threshold, and a contrast sensitivity function records that quantity across spatial frequencies.

claims.causal_estimand: Within-protocol change in contrast-detection threshold produced by changing grating spatial frequency or waveform while following the reported psychophysical procedure.

confidence.rationale: The source reports repeated controlled psychophysical comparisons across frequencies and waveforms, but it is a historical study with limited modern reporting and protocol-specific generalizability.

limitations: The experiment identifies effects of stimulus properties on task thresholds, not a unique neural channel, normalization process, or complete account of visual perception.
claims.plain_language_summary: In the classic experiments, the researchers changed how wide the light and dark stripes were and measured how much contrast people needed to see them. The required contrast changed systematically with stripe spacing and waveform. This establishes an effect of the tested image properties on detection in that procedure, but it does not reveal one unique brain mechanism.

boundary_conditions: Periodic gratings, the reported spatial-frequency range, waveform comparisons, adaptation, luminance, viewing geometry, and threshold procedure.
scope.population: Human observers tested in the Campbell and Robson 1968 grating experiments.
scope.temporal_scope: Stimulus presentation through the observer's detection response and threshold estimate.

claims.statement: In the Campbell and Robson experiments, controlled changes in grating spatial frequency and waveform produced systematic differences in contrast-detection thresholds.
claims.temporal_ordering: The experimenter set grating properties before each detection response and threshold estimate.

confidence.rationale: The model explains a broad set of visual-cortex response properties and is supported by physiological literature, but the cited evidence does not uniquely identify its biological implementation or directly establish the human psychophysical pathway.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The account is weakened if preregistered comparisons show that normalization models fail to predict held-out neural and psychophysical contrast responses better than plausible non-normalizing alternatives.
limitations: Model fit is not proof of a unique causal circuit, and nonhuman cortical physiology is indirect evidence for human contrast-detection behavior.
claims.plain_language_summary: A proposed neural explanation is that a visual neuron’s response is scaled down by the combined activity of a larger pool of neurons, preventing responses from growing without limit as contrast increases. This model explains many visual-cortex findings, especially in nonhuman physiology, but it has not been shown here to be the unique cause of the human contrast-sensitivity curve.

boundary_conditions: A specified normalization pool and model must predict contrast-response or threshold data beyond simpler alternatives.
scope.population: Visual systems studied with contrast-varying stimuli, including cat visual cortex and human psychophysics.
scope.temporal_scope: Stimulus-driven neural response through contrast-dependent behavioral detection.

claims.statement: Divisive normalization may shape visual response gain and thereby contribute to contrast-dependent neural and behavioral sensitivity.
claims.temporal_ordering: Visual stimulation precedes pooled gain regulation, neural response, and any later behavioral threshold estimate.

families.description: Visual perception, contrast sensitivity, grating manipulation, detection response, threshold measurement, and divisive normalization kept distinct.

effect.notes: Thresholds varied systematically with spatial frequency, and near threshold the fundamental Fourier component accounted for visibility across tested waveforms.

evidence.extraction_locator: Abstract points 1-5 and full report of contrast thresholds across spatial frequencies and sine, square, rectangular, and saw-tooth gratings.
limitations: Historical methods and reporting do not meet current preregistration and open-data standards, and the result is tied to the tested stimuli and viewing conditions.
evidence.population: Human observers in the reported laboratory experiments; a pooled participant count was not extracted from the article.
evidence.summary: Controlled changes to spatial frequency and waveform changed the contrast required for human observers to detect gratings.

evidence.design: Computational normalization model evaluated against a reviewed body of physiological measurements from cat striate cortex.

effect.metric: breadth of striate-cell response properties explained by the modified model
effect.notes: Adding mutual inhibition or response normalization explained more physiological findings than the unnormalized linear-energy account.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract describing the modified linear-energy model and its account of published cat striate-cortex response properties.
limitations: This is model-based nonhuman neural evidence, not a randomized perturbation of normalization and not direct evidence about human detection thresholds.
evidence.population: Neurons and physiological datasets from cat striate cortex reviewed and modeled in the article.
evidence.summary: A normalization model accounted for a broader set of cat visual-cortex response properties than an unnormalized linear-energy model.

evidence.design: Narrative synthesis of computational and physiological normalization findings across neural systems and species.

effect.metric: cross-system explanatory applicability of normalization models
effect.notes: The review presents normalization as a promising canonical computation while noting multiple model variants and unresolved biological implementations.

evidence.extraction_locator: Abstract and Box 1 defining the normalization equation, its normalization pool, fitted parameters, and applications across visual and other neural systems.
limitations: Narrative synthesis and broad cross-system fit do not establish one implementation or a direct causal path to the human contrast sensitivity function.
evidence.population: Neural systems and experimental preparations across multiple species, with emphasis on visual-system evidence.
evidence.summary: A cross-system review supports normalization as a widely useful candidate neural computation, not as one uniquely established circuit.

limitations: The definition does not establish that one task validly measures all forms of deduction or that formal correctness identifies one psychological mechanism.
claims.plain_language_summary: Deductive reasoning asks whether a conclusion must follow if the stated premises are accepted. This defines a kind of reasoning; it does not say that one syllogism score measures all reasoning or identifies how the mind reaches the answer.

scope.population: Humans constructing or evaluating deductive arguments.
scope.temporal_scope: Premise representation through conclusion evaluation.

claims.statement: Deductive reasoning constructs or evaluates arguments intended to show that a conclusion necessarily follows from premises or hypotheses.

claims.causal_estimand: Within-protocol difference in conclusion endorsement produced by changing conclusion believability across valid and invalid syllogisms.

confidence.rationale: Three controlled experiments reproduced the validity-by-believability pattern with several response-bias controls, but the historical samples and task materials limit generalization.

limitations: The effect concerns endorsement in these tasks and does not prove that participants ignored logic or identify a unique cognitive process.
claims.plain_language_summary: People were more likely to accept a conclusion when it sounded believable, even though they were asked to judge whether it followed logically from the premises. The effect was stronger for invalid arguments. This shows that content changed responses in those tasks, not that participants had no logical information.

boundary_conditions: The reported categorical syllogisms, believable and unbelievable conclusions, logical-validity classifications, instructions, and response procedures.
scope.population: Human participants in three syllogistic-reasoning experiments reported by Evans, Barston, and Pollard in 1983.
scope.temporal_scope: Argument presentation through verbal protocol and validity judgment.

claims.statement: In the Evans, Barston, and Pollard experiments, manipulated conclusion believability changed syllogism endorsement, with a larger belief bias for invalid than valid arguments.
claims.temporal_ordering: The experimenter-defined premises and conclusion properties were presented before the participant's judgment.

confidence.rationale: The analysis included 993 participants and modeled participant and item heterogeneity, but conclusions depend on the signal-detection specification and available confidence-rating studies.

claims.confounding_note: Study designs, item sets, participant heterogeneity, response scales, and model assumptions can change the decomposition of discrimination and criterion effects.

estimate.metric: group-level discriminability for believable versus unbelievable syllogisms
estimate.notes: The meta-analysis reported no unconditional effect of believability on discriminability, while allowing conditional effects associated with individual differences.

limitations: This result does not mean that believability never changes judgments; it distinguishes unconditional validity discrimination from response bias and conditional effects.
claims.plain_language_summary: A reanalysis of 22 studies separated two things that raw accuracy can mix: detecting which arguments are valid and being more willing to accept believable conclusions. Believability changed response tendencies, but it did not generally reduce validity discrimination across everyone and every item.

boundary_conditions: Studies with confidence-rating or compatible response data included in the hierarchical signal-detection corpus.
scope.population: 993 participants represented in 22 syllogistic confidence-rating studies reanalyzed by Trippas and colleagues.
scope.temporal_scope: Confidence-rated validity judgments aggregated across the included studies.

claims.statement: In a hierarchical signal-detection meta-analysis of 22 confidence-rating studies, conclusion believability did not unconditionally reduce discrimination between valid and invalid syllogisms.

confidence.rationale: Behavioral interference and autonomic evidence support concurrent conflict in some tasks, but recent experiments show that experimenter-defined logical conflict can mismatch participants' subjective representations.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The account is weakened when preregistered process measures show no mutual interference or conflict-sensitive change after subjective argument interpretation is measured and plausible single-process alternatives fit held-out responses better.
limitations: Conflict effects do not establish two discrete mental systems, and the same response pattern can arise from different representations or strategies.
claims.plain_language_summary: One proposed explanation is that the mind can begin evaluating both plausibility and logical structure at the same time. When they suggest different answers, processing may become slower, less confident, or more arousing. Recent experiments show that researchers cannot assume every formally invalid argument creates this subjective conflict, so the mechanism remains conditional and proposed.

boundary_conditions: Participants must represent both content-based and structural cues; objective and subjective conflict cannot be assumed equivalent.
scope.population: Humans evaluating syllogistic arguments in which conclusion believability and experimenter-defined validity agree or conflict.
scope.temporal_scope: Argument encoding through response selection and confidence judgment.

claims.statement: Belief-based and logic-based evaluations may sometimes proceed in parallel and generate response conflict when they favor different judgments.
claims.temporal_ordering: Content and argument structure are processed after presentation and before the final validity judgment.

families.description: Deductive construct, syllogism task, validity and believability, judgments, performance, signal detection, and parallel evaluation kept distinct.

evidence.design: Three controlled syllogistic-reasoning experiments varying conclusion validity and believability with response-bias controls.

effect.metric: conclusion endorsement by validity and believability condition
effect.notes: Believable conclusions were endorsed more often, logical validity also strongly affected judgments, and belief bias was larger for invalid than valid syllogisms.

evidence.extraction_locator: Abstract and three experiment reports crossing conclusion believability with logical validity and analyzing verbal protocols.
limitations: Historical experiments lacked preregistration and modern multilevel item analysis, and verbal protocols do not uniquely reveal latent processes.
evidence.population: Human participants in the three reported experiments; one pooled sample size was not extracted.
evidence.summary: Three experiments found that both logical validity and conclusion believability influenced syllogism judgments, with stronger belief bias on invalid arguments.

evidence.design: Hierarchical Bayesian signal-detection meta-analysis of receiver-operating-characteristic data plus corroborating experimental design.

effect.metric: unconditional believable-versus-unbelievable difference in validity discriminability
effect.notes: Believability did not influence discriminability unconditionally; individual-difference factors could condition the effect.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract and hierarchical signal-detection reanalysis of 22 confidence-rating studies.
limitations: The corpus and inference depend on included confidence-rating studies and the hierarchical signal-detection model.
evidence.population: 993 participants across 22 confidence-rating studies.
evidence.summary: A hierarchical meta-analysis separated response criterion from validity discrimination and found no unconditional believability effect on discriminability.

evidence.design: Two experiments manipulating judgment instruction, belief-logic conflict, and argument complexity while measuring accuracy, response time, and confidence.

effect.metric: mutual interference between logical validity and believability judgments
effect.notes: The direction and size of interference depended on argument complexity, consistent with concurrent belief- and logic-based processing rather than a fixed fast-belief slow-logic sequence.

evidence.extraction_locator: Abstract and general discussion of two experiments comparing validity and believability judgments across argument complexity.
limitations: Interference patterns are indirect process evidence and depend on task complexity, instructions, and model comparison.
evidence.population: Human participants completing deductive arguments under validity-judgment or believability-judgment instructions.
evidence.summary: Two experiments found complexity-dependent mutual interference between logical and belief judgments, supporting but not proving parallel evaluation.

evidence.design: Syllogistic-reasoning experiment measuring autonomic arousal when intuitive believability agreed or conflicted with the logically classified response.

effect.metric: skin-conductance response during conflict versus no-conflict reasoning
effect.notes: Conflict problems elicited greater autonomic response, including among participants who ultimately gave belief-biased answers.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract and experiment report comparing skin-conductance responses during conflict and no-conflict syllogisms.
limitations: Skin conductance is not specific to logical conflict and does not identify parallel evaluation as the only generating process.
evidence.population: University participants solving conflict and no-conflict syllogisms while skin conductance was recorded.
evidence.summary: Greater skin conductance during belief-logic conflict was consistent with implicit conflict sensitivity even when final judgments were biased.

evidence.design: Two experiments comparing experimenter-defined and subjectively represented conflict in conditional syllogistic inferences.

effect.metric: response-time and confidence conflict-detection indices after chosen response was considered
effect.notes: Expected conflict differences were generally absent after believability and chosen response were considered; some apparent conflict was better described as competition between heuristic responses.

evidence.extraction_locator: Abstract and analyses from two experiments testing invalid conditional inferences, response time, confidence, and subjective conflict classification.
limitations: The challenge concerns particular invalid conditional inferences and does not rule out belief-logic conflict in every reasoning task.
evidence.population: 248 human participants across two experiments.
evidence.summary: Two recent experiments showed that objective logical conflict can mismatch subjective conflict and challenged a universal logic-versus-heuristic interpretation.

boundary_notes: Deductive reasoning is broader than performance on one syllogism task and narrower than thinking or intelligence in general.

objects.definition: Experimental crossing of whether a conclusion is logically entailed by its premises and whether it is believable from prior world knowledge.
objects.delivery: Present protocol-defined valid and invalid arguments with believable and unbelievable conclusions, including conflict and no-conflict combinations.
objects.label: Syllogism validity-believability manipulation

objects.definition: Observable acceptance or rejection of a conclusion as following logically from the presented premises.
objects.function_note: An endorsement can reflect logical analysis, conclusion believability, response criterion, misunderstanding, or a mixture of processes.
objects.label: Syllogism validity judgment
objects.response_topography: Protocol-defined keypress, rating, or verbal response indicating that the conclusion follows or does not follow.

boundary_notes: Accuracy depends on the selected normative logic, argument interpretation, item content, and response procedure.
objects.definition: Protocol-scored agreement between a participant's validity judgment and the formal validity classification of the argument.
objects.label: Syllogistic judgment performance

boundary_notes: Raw acceptance or accuracy does not by itself separate validity discrimination from a tendency to accept believable conclusions.
objects.definition: Acceptance rates, rejection rates, accuracy, response time, confidence, or verbal protocols summarized separately by validity and believability condition.
objects.label: Condition-specific syllogism judgments
objects.method: Record each validity judgment and prespecified process measures, then compare valid, invalid, believable, unbelievable, conflict, and no-conflict conditions.

boundary_notes: Discriminability and criterion are model-dependent estimates, not direct observations of reasoning mechanisms.
Aggregating heterogeneous people or items can distort receiver-operating-characteristic interpretations.
objects.definition: Model-based separation of sensitivity to argument validity from response criteria using endorsement and confidence distributions for valid and invalid syllogisms.
objects.label: Syllogistic signal-detection profile
objects.method: Fit a declared signal-detection model to participant- and item-level endorsement or confidence data and estimate discriminability and response criteria by condition.

boundary_notes: Parallel evaluation is a process hypothesis, not another name for a validity-by-believability interaction.
Slower responses, lower confidence, skin conductance, or mutual interference are indirect and non-unique indicators of conflict.
objects.definition: Proposed process in which content-based plausibility and argument-structure information are evaluated concurrently and can support compatible or competing responses.
objects.label: Parallel belief-logic evaluation
realization_conditions: The participant extracts enough content and structural information for both evaluations to influence processing.
Conflict measures distinguish subjective response competition from experimenter-assigned logical conflict.

action.en: First ask whether the conclusion must follow if the premises are accepted; only afterward evaluate whether the premises and conclusion are realistic. Restating the structure with neutral symbols is a candidate aid.
action.ru: Сначала спросите, обязан ли вывод следовать из принятых посылок, и только затем оценивайте реалистичность посылок и вывода. Перезапись структуры нейтральными символами может помочь, но пока это лишь кандидатный приём.

applicability.en: Candidate checklist for education, analysis, and review of short deductive arguments.
applicability.ru: Кандидатный чек-лист для обучения, анализа и проверки коротких дедуктивных аргументов.

evidence_basis.en: Experiments show that manipulated believability changes validity judgments, but the mapped pack does not directly test this debiasing procedure.
evidence_basis.ru: Эксперименты показывают, что изменение правдоподобия влияет на оценку валидности, но представленный пакет напрямую не проверяет эту процедуру снижения ошибки.

expected_change.en: The intended change is less contamination of validity judgments by conclusion believability.
expected_change.ru: Предполагаемый результат — меньшее влияние правдоподобия вывода на оценку логической валидности.

not_established.en: It is not established here that the checklist reliably reduces bias, generalizes to real decisions, or changes an underlying reasoning mechanism.
not_established.ru: Здесь не доказано, что чек-лист надёжно снижает ошибку, переносится на реальные решения или изменяет внутренний механизм рассуждения.

practical_question.en: How might a person reduce the influence of a believable conclusion when checking an argument?
practical_question.ru: Как можно уменьшить влияние правдоподобного вывода при проверке аргумента?

title.en: Separate logical validity from plausibility
title.ru: Отделяйте логическую валидность от правдоподобия

question.en: When do people actually represent a conflict between logic and believability, and which process model predicts it?
question.ru: Когда человек действительно воспринимает конфликт между логикой и правдоподобием и какая модель процесса его предсказывает?

what_would_help.en: Preregistered experiments measuring participants' argument representations and comparing competing process models on held-out person- and item-level data.
what_would_help.ru: Пререгистрированные эксперименты, измеряющие представление аргумента участником и сравнивающие конкурирующие модели процесса на отложенных данных по людям и заданиям.

why_open.en: Experimenter-defined invalidity can differ from subjective conflict, and response time, confidence, or arousal do not uniquely identify parallel processing.
why_open.ru: Заданная исследователем невалидность может не совпадать с субъективным конфликтом, а время ответа, уверенность и возбуждение не выявляют однозначно параллельную обработку.
